name: Tsang 2004: six counter-clockwise rotations of the Thomas pattern (30 min)
origin: Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004 (Laurentian University), circumcerebral "Octopus" ring
summary: All six configurations of Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004 in the table's order, 5 min each: the 849-point Thomas pattern at 1-ms points, stepped counter-clockwise round the ring with a dwell that shortens or lengthens at each position. The paper reports more 35-45 Hz power over frontal and occipital sites during the third one only (25 ms shortening to 11 ms).
notes: Tsang 2004 writes + for a dwell that gets shorter: 100 ms falling by 10 ms per position to 30 ms, 100 rising to 170, 25 falling to 11, 25 rising to 39, 167 falling to 27, 167 rising to 307 (Table 1 p.4 [1186]; p.5 [1187]). The pattern had 849 points of 1 ms with 1 ms between repeats (p.5 [1187]). The EEG was taken for 20 s, 2.5 min into each configuration. This program plays those values as published, in the table's order, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2, with the 849-point table of US 6,234,953. The ring had two solenoids per position; this helmet has one coil. The first solenoid was over the left frontal region and the eighth over the right prefrontal region (p.4 [1186]); the site names are this project's reading. The paper gives 0.5 to 1.5 uT near the scalp (p.5 [1187]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT the scalp gets about 24 uT, 16 to 48 times the paper's value; about 0.04 uT matches it. Eleven people and one significant configuration of six. It was always the third, and the paper says a cumulative effect of the fixed order cannot be excluded (p.10 [1192]). The amplifier filters were set between 0.5 and 35 Hz for a 35 to 45 Hz measure (p.6 [1188]), and the EEG was sampled with the field on. Single lab, never independently replicated.
setting: Seated, eyes closed, in a quiet, dim room. To check the gamma claim, record EEG over frontal and occipital sites and take a 20-s sample 2.5 min in.
source: Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004, Power increases within the gamma range over the frontal and occipital regions during acute exposures to cerebrally counterclockwise rotating magnetic fields with specific derivatives of change, Int J Neurosci 114:1183-1193 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15370182/ ; Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:877-894 (six 5-min ring configurations, 1 microTesla range) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738355/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Saroka 2016, PhD dissertation, Laurentian University (Cook 1999 rotated the Thomas pulse with "the Octopus") https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/be015982-0b0f-4c27-a031-797637c364e1/content ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4) (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
